# Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#spider2)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.07763v2) · arXiv v2, 17 March 2025; ICLR 2025 version

**Reading coverage:** All 45 PDF pages: main sections 1–6; Appendix A evaluation scripts; B.1–B.8 annotation, SQL examples, context, documentation and statistics; C.1–C.7 experiments, error analysis, costs, trajectories and prompts. Figure 13 rendered for its embedded document.

## Research question

Conventional SQL benchmarks underrepresent large schemas, dialect differences, external business definitions and repository-level data transformation workflows.

## Method

Spider 2.0 combines rewritten public SQL and incomplete dbt projects with database access, documentation, executable interfaces and task-specific outputs. Spider-Agent explores files and schemas, writes and executes queries, and iteratively repairs its work. Lite and Snow variants isolate SQL generation under different environments.

## Evaluation

The paper evaluates 632 workflow problems and 547 SQL-only problems using task-specific success tests or focused execution matching. The scorer can ignore extra columns and selected ordering differences. Model comparisons, error analysis, oracle-function and few-shot interventions, and matched cross-dialect examples probe the difficulty.

## What the results support

The reported o1-preview Spider-Agent solves 21.36% of workflows. Errors include planning, schema linking, nested fields and grounding external definitions; reference function documentation and a few demonstrations provide limited improvements. These are results for the paper’s dated models and harnesses.

## Limits and qualifications

Lite deliberately reduces ambiguity, whereas workflow tasks may resolve underspecification through supplied context and selective scoring. No dedicated clarification or unanswerability test is established. Cloud costs, omitted value retrieval in baseline adaptations, and different harness settings constrain comparison. Focused output matching is not a proof of full semantic equivalence.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A realistic adjacent stress test for contextual grounding and agent workflows, useful for studying where reliable SQL generation fails before adding explicit answerability or clarification evaluation.
